ruleset.name: WPHEKA Quality default
ruleset.description:
WordPress Coding Standards with formatting-only sniffs removed.
This is the ruleset the engine uses when a repository does not ship its own. It exists because the engine's job is to surface defects that matter, and layout findings drown them.
Measured on a real plugin: the full WordPress standard produced 1427 findings, of which roughly 1200 were indentation, alignment and bracket spacing. Underneath them sat 32 missing or recommended nonce checks, 17 unescaped outputs and 7 direct database queries. A reviewer reading that report top to bottom meets 582 space-vs-tab findings first.
Nothing here judges code quality. Every sniff removed below reports on the shape of the source rather than its behaviour, and none of them can describe a bug. Formatting is a job for phpcbf and an editor config, not for a review that is looking for security and correctness defects.
Run with --all-sniffs to use config/phpcs-all-sniffs.xml instead, which applies the WordPress standard untouched. A repository's own phpcs.xml always takes precedence over both.
